pr.title: Say a stacked layer merged with its stack into the default branch, not only into the branch below it
pr.head: 37bf2716a4c6aa1cc5cc79c4f20074b44f2d676e

summary: Projector's watch daemon polls the pull requests a session subscribes to and tells the session about each event as one line. When a pull request merges, the line is MERGED owner/repo#N into <base> at …, and the agent that reads it decides what to tell the person.

A stack is a chain of pull requests, each based on the branch of the one below it. GitHub records each upper layer as merged into the branch below it, even when the whole stack merged into the default branch as a unit. Agents reading into layer-5 concluded the change missed main and told the person so.
This pull request makes the daemon check, for a merged pull request whose base is not the default branch, whether that base reached the default branch, and word the line to match:

• MERGED … with its stack into main at … when the layers below merged into the default branch.
  • MERGED … into layer-5 at …, which is not in main yet when a layer below is open or the stack is based on another branch.
  • The old wording, unchanged, for a pull request based on the default branch, or when GitHub cannot say.
The review found one open problem: the check never compares merge times, so a layer merged into a branch whose own pull request merged earlier is reported as landed in main.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Layer: one pull request of a stack.
  • GitHub stack: the stack GitHub records through repos/<repo>/stacks?pull_request=N, with its base.ref and each layer's merged_at.
  • Chain: layers linked only by base branches, where GitHub records no stack.
  • Pass: one round of the daemon's polling; a per-pass memo answers each question once a round.

cards.title: What it costs
cards.html:
• The pass query also reads defaultBranchRef, at no extra request.
  • A pull request based on the default branch makes no request.
  • A merged layer reads GitHub's stack once a pass, shared with the fixer-name lookup and every other layer.
  • A chain asks pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>&state=all once per branch, only at a merge.

groups.title: Wording MERGED for a layer
groups.kicker: How the daemon decides whether a merged layer reached the default branch
intro: closed_detail now builds the MERGED or CLOSED line, and only once a pass for the first session that needs it. When the base is neither unknown nor the default branch, it asks landed, which returns True, False, or None when nothing answers.

landed tries GitHub's stack first: when the pull request is a layer of it, the answer is whether the stack is based on the default branch and every layer below has a merged_at. Otherwise it walks the chain down by head branch, returning False on an open pull request and following each merged one's base until it reaches the default branch.

The stack request moved from Daemon.stack into Daemon.read_stack, and the per-pass github_stack memo records the answer for every layer it lists. bottom, which names a stack's fixer subagent, reads through the same memo. The four copies of the gh api JSON parsing became json_of.

checks.text: The stack API's shape matches what landed reads: a live repos/ninjudd/projector/stacks answer carries base.ref and each layer's merged_at, and records a stack merged as a unit with each layer a second after the one below.

files.note: The new closed_detail, landed, github_stack, and pulls_headed on Pass, and read_stack split out of Daemon.stack.

checks.text: landed counts a layer below as carrying this one whenever it has a merged_at, without comparing it with this pull request's mergedAt. When #5 merged into main and kept its branch, and #6 merged into layer-5 later, the daemon says with its stack into main though #6's change is only on the dead branch. The stack path at line 1686 has the same gap. A scratch test reproduced it.
bottom keeps its freshness cache in daemon.stacks, and now reads the stack through the per-pass memo, so a merge and its fixer name share one request; the new cost test passed in the gate.

files.note: The fake's stacks and head lookups gain merged_at, base, and state=all, and five StackFixerTests cover each wording and the request counts.

groups.title: Documenting the wording
groups.kicker: What docs/cli.md and fix-pr tell a reader and an agent
intro: docs/cli.md shows both new forms with what each means and costs, and the event table says MERGED now reports whether a layer's base reached the default branch. fix-pr, the skill a fixer session follows, says what each form means so its agent does not misreport a merge.
